summary: Audit custody and hashes verify exactly; the demonstrated post-commit defect, queue-ordering causality, recovery-owner claim (Q1: correct — recovery reconciles the exact row once, no schema/API/wire/dependency needed), the three-check coverage of both close orderings (Q2), operationAdmissionHalted as owner (Q3: correct for committedFailure paths; terminal ambiguity is separately fail-closed via terminalState), RED causality through the real issue/store/close path with a one-use journal adapter (Q4), and GREEN acceptance of exact-once recovery, policy reconstruction, 0→1→2 continuation and non-null retirement boundary (Q5) all hold. One material failure ordering is missing (Q6): a non-terminal transactIssue throw classified ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN — a contract-sanctioned possibly-committed outcome — sets no flag when no operation policy is installed, so the same close-omits-durable-row defect survives the frozen GREEN on no-policy planes. The fix is a small extension of the same seam, not a redesign.

findings.title: Ambiguous transactIssue outcome (ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) escapes unconditional halt on no-policy planes
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5682-5699 (catch sets operationAdmissionHalted only via `else if (reservation !== undefined)` when signerResolved && !terminalTransactionStarted); packages/issuance-store/src/terminal.ts:111-126 (classifyDurableIssuanceTerminalSuppression throws UnknownOutcomeFailure when the commit may have landed but readback is unreadable, and returns the commit when durable rows prove success at :153-163); packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:748-776 (real ambiguous-throw path); packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:801-819 (committing-failure readback path). Plan GREEN item 1 (docs/.../production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:96241-96243) is scoped to 'after issuer.issue() returned' and the fault matrix (:96294-96298) lists only committedFailure positions; 'failure before journal write' denotes post-commit pre-journal committedFailure cases (v3-live.ts:5711-5760), not a pre-return ambiguous transaction throw.
findings.impact: On a creator plane without an operation admission policy, a transactIssue throw with ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN can leave a durable issued/pending-outbox row while the issue reports 'issuance-rejected: v3 local issue transaction failed', no recovery-required flag is set, and neither close check (items 2-3) fires — the queued or later close folds a graph omitting the durable row, reproducing the exact demonstrated defect (omitted orphan row freezes later closes per the D.110c-0c1a derivation) after GREEN passes. Incorrect code therefore passes the frozen acceptance for a supported no-policy configuration.
findings.required_action: Amend GREEN item 1 so the existing flag is also set unconditionally when the non-terminal issue transaction outcome is ambiguous: bind the caught error at v3-live.ts:5682 and set registration.operationAdmissionHalted whenever the thrown error carries code ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, independent of reservation presence (do not flag the definitely-pre-commit capacityRejected throw, which never reaches the store commit). Add 'issuance transaction outcome unknown (non-terminal, no policy)' to the focused fault matrix with the same close-refusal and recover-exactly-once assertions. No new schema, API, wire field, dependency, or store operation is required; the RED journal-rejection witness remains causal and unchanged.

findings.title: Unconditional flag set silently widens halt to ingress and no-policy issue paths
findings.evidence: v3-live.ts:3727 (handleV3Ingress rejects new admissions when operationAdmissionHalted) and :5600-5602 (issueOneVertex rejects); GREEN item 1 makes the flag reachable for planes without an operation policy for the first time, so post-commit failures on such planes now halt all subsequent ingress and local issue until deactivate+recovery — a behavioral consequence the plan text does not enumerate (it discusses only close refusal).
findings.impact: A retained suite that exercises a post-commit failure without a policy and expects continued ingress/issue could newly fail; conversely the broadening is fail-closed and consistent with the flag's existing meaning, so no incorrect close can pass.
findings.required_action: Owner: GREEN implementer. Disposition: no plan-text change required; the frozen retained gates (E5-01 admission/recovery, D.110c-a/b hot path, issuance/outbox suites) are the check — if any retained test depends on post-failure continuation without a policy, that is exactly the plan's stated stop-and-reslice trigger rather than a silent pass.

findings.title: Fold-time refusal leaves blueprintClosing latched; acceptance should pin the in-memory wedge
findings.evidence: v3-live.ts:6713 sets registration.blueprintClosing = true synchronously before the queued recheck in stageClosedBlueprintEpoch would refuse; the only in-memory clearing is abortSnapshotStage (v3-live.ts:6991-6996), and with the flag set every subsequent creatorCloseRegistration refuses, so the plane remains open-but-unclosable until deactivation plus recovery creates a fresh registration (v3-live.ts:7263-7310 with operationAdmissionHalted: false).
findings.impact: Intended fail-closed behavior, and the GREEN text's 'neither refusal may change durable head, snapshot, graph, application state, or the surviving row' is not violated (the latch is in-memory only); but an acceptance test could accidentally assume the refusal unwinds blueprintClosing or consumes the close claim (it does not — claimedCreatorCloseHandles is only marked on a successful mint, v3-live.ts:2590-2591).
findings.required_action: Owner: GREEN test author. Disposition: assert explicitly that the refused close leaves durable state untouched, that the close claim is not consumed by a refused mint (post-recovery close on the fresh registration succeeds — already implied by the 0→1 continuation), and that abortSnapshotStage remains the only in-memory abort; no production-code or plan-scope change.
